_comment: Mutations that put the FORK's screener/symbol-feed WebSocket
configuration back the way the fork had it.
This repo is a FORK of DepthSight-Pro/DepthSight and had lost the env
overrides on MAIN_APP_WS_URL and SYMBOL_SOURCE_MODE, had INVERTED the
MAIN_APP_WS_ENABLED default to 'true', and hardcoded the UPSTREAM's own
reserved hostname (screener.depthsight.pro) as the URL. That URL is not
this fork's deployment, it answers HTTP 525, and NOTHING in this fork
produces the 'active_pairs_update' message the bot's screener client
expects -- so the feed can never work here, and a DYNAMIC-mode strategy
started against it reports 'running' and silently never trades.
F1/F2/F3 put those three regressions back.
F4/F5/F12 break the shared rules in bot_module/screener_feed.py.
F6/F7/F8 remove one of the three doors that must refuse a DYNAMIC
strategy in the UNSAFE PAIRING (the consumer, the bot's Redis command
channel, and the HTTP route).
F9/F10/F11/F13 are the FALSE-POSITIVE mutations: they make the guard
refuse deployments that WOULD have worked, or stop it refusing the ones
that would not. Both directions must be caught.
ROUND 2 INVERTED F11.  It used to pin 'the SAFE pairing (feed off,
URL empty) is NOT misconfigured', which was true then and is FALSE
now: with the feed switched off there is no symbol source at all (the
DYNAMIC symbol pool is filled only by the feed's 'active_pairs_update'
message, controller.py:7216) and there is no fallback to the static
list, so a DYNAMIC strategy started there reports 'running' and never
trades.  The guarantee is now the OPPOSITE one -- the feed-off pairing
MUST be refused -- and F11 is the mutant that takes it away again.
The delivery rules added in round 2 have their own spec:
tools/mutations/screener_ws_delivery_guard.json.
Run with:  python tools/mutation_harness.py tools/mutations/fork_screener_ws_config.json
NEVER run concurrently with a test run or tools/review_fanout.py -- both will
read a file that is mid-mutation and report on code that does not exist.
